implementation_notes: JavaScript has no parameter type, so the pattern degenerates into one object parameter that the callee destructures in its signature (`function drawEdge({ x, y, width = 1 })`); property defaults replace overloads and JSDoc `@param {{x: number}}` documents the shape. The classic class with a constructor is only justified once the group needs validation or behaviour, or when the same object is passed between many modules and a name helps debugging.
pitfalls: A mistyped property name is `undefined` at runtime with no warning; validate or use TypeScript/JSDoc for non-trivial carriers.
An options object is easy to grow into a junk drawer because adding a property never breaks a caller - review the group's cohesion.
Destructuring discards the object, so a forwarding wrapper must keep the parameter itself (`function f(params) { const { x } = params; g(params); }`).
